speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To better understand your condition, how long have you been experiencing this swelling and pain in your right ring finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant trauma. Did you hear a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to make a full fist with your other fingers?

REQUEST TEST: X_Ray_right_hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: It seems there has been a significant misunderstanding; Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and cannot cause finger injuries. Based on your description of a "pop," inability to flex the distal joint, and the finger resting in extension, I suspect a mallet finger or avulsion fracture. Please confirm if you have noticed any visible deformity or bruising at the tip of your finger.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (likely with an associated avulsion fracture).

REQUEST IMAGES: X_Ray_right_hand_distal_interphalangeal_joint_LATERAL_AND_OBLIQUE

Based on your inability to actively flex the tip of your finger and the history of trauma, I suspect a tendon avulsion. The X-ray images will help confirm if there is a fracture at the base of the nail.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
